title: Memory, Concurrency, and Scheduling
description: Page tables, the TLB, locks, races, and the scheduler that lies about how many CPUs you have.

sourceReferences.title: xv6 book
sourceReferences.notes: Page tables, then locks, then scheduling.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.1810
sourceReferences.notes: Labs extend VM and concurrency after the kernel is thinkable.

modules.title: Virtual memory
learningObjectives: Treat an address as a translation the hardware walks
Treat a missing translation as a request, not only a crash

modules.title: Scheduling
learningObjectives: Choose which runnable thread owns a core next

modules.title: Synchronization
learningObjectives: Name a race as order-dependent results
Use a lock as one holder at a time

concepts.name: Virtual memory
concepts.summary: Pages, page tables, and the TLB as a cache of translations.
objectives: Describe virtual memory as translating process addresses to physical frames
Predict what a program sees when two processes use the same virtual address

concepts.name: Page tables
concepts.summary: A tree of translations the hardware walks.
objectives: Describe a page table as the tree the hardware walks to translate a page
Predict why a multi-level table can stay sparse

concepts.name: TLB shootdown
concepts.summary: When one core changes a mapping, the others must forget.
objectives: Explain a TLB shootdown as forcing other cores to drop a stale translation
Predict what happens if one core changes a mapping and the others keep the old TLB entry

concepts.name: Page faults
concepts.summary: A missing translation as a request, not only a crash.
objectives: Describe a page fault as a missing translation that transfers into the kernel
Distinguish a fault that should fill a page from one that should kill the process

concepts.name: Paging to disk
concepts.summary: The illusion of more RAM than you bought.
objectives: Explain paging to disk as evicting a frame and bringing it back on the next fault
Predict the cost of treating the disk as extra RAM when many processes miss

concepts.name: Copy-on-write
concepts.summary: fork that does not copy until a write.
objectives: Describe copy-on-write as sharing frames after fork until a write
Predict which mapping changes when one side writes a shared page

concepts.name: mmap
concepts.summary: A file, or anonymous memory, appearing as a range of addresses.
objectives: Describe mmap as making a file or anonymous memory appear as a range of addresses
Predict what a load from that range does before the bytes are in RAM

concepts.name: CPU scheduling
concepts.summary: Fairness, latency, and why CFS is not a real-time scheduler.
objectives: Describe the scheduler as choosing which runnable thread owns a core next
Contrast a fair-share policy with one that tries to meet a deadline

concepts.name: Fair-share scheduling
concepts.summary: Who is owed the next slice.
objectives: Explain fair-share as each task being owed a slice weighted by its share
Predict who runs next when one task has consumed more than its share

concepts.name: Latency versus throughput in the scheduler
concepts.summary: Interactive tails versus batch work.
objectives: Contrast scheduler choices that cut wakeup latency with those that maximize throughput
Predict why a batch job can wreck an interactive tail

concepts.name: Real-time scheduling
concepts.summary: Deadlines, not averages.
objectives: Describe real-time scheduling as meeting deadlines, not averages
Predict why a fair-share scheduler is the wrong tool for a deadline

concepts.name: Scheduling classes
concepts.summary: More than one policy living in one kernel.
objectives: Describe scheduling classes as more than one policy living in one kernel
Predict which class wins when a real-time task and a fair-share task are both runnable

concepts.name: Load balancing
concepts.summary: Moving work across cores without wrecking caches.
objectives: Describe load balancing as moving work across cores
Predict the cache cost of bouncing a thread to a colder core

concepts.name: NUMA awareness
concepts.summary: Memory that is closer to some cores than others.
objectives: Explain NUMA as memory that is closer to some cores than others
Predict why running a thread far from its pages costs more than a local miss

concepts.name: Preemption
concepts.summary: Taking the CPU back.
objectives: Describe preemption as taking the CPU back from a running thread
Predict what must be saved when the kernel interrupts a thread that did not yield

concepts.name: Priority inversion
concepts.summary: A low task holding a lock a high task needs.
objectives: Diagnose priority inversion as a low task holding a lock a high task needs
Predict a fix that lets the low task finish without the high task waiting behind a middle one

concepts.name: Locks
concepts.summary: Mutual exclusion as a primitive, not a vibe.
objectives: Describe a lock as mutual exclusion: one holder at a time
Predict what goes wrong if two threads update the same structure without a lock

concepts.name: Sleeping locks
concepts.summary: Blocking instead of spinning when the hold is long.
objectives: Contrast a sleeping lock with spinning while the holder runs
Predict when spinning wastes the core and sleeping is cheaper

concepts.name: Deadlock
concepts.summary: Everyone waiting for someone who is waiting for them.
objectives: Describe deadlock as everyone waiting for someone who is waiting for them
Diagnose a two-lock cycle from the order two threads acquire

concepts.name: Races
concepts.summary: A result that depends on who ran first.
objectives: Describe a race as a result that depends on who ran first
Diagnose a lost update when two threads read-modify-write the same word

concepts.name: Atomics
concepts.summary: Read-modify-write that does not tear.
objectives: Describe an atomic as a read-modify-write that does not tear
Predict which updates still race even if each store is atomic

concepts.name: Memory ordering for programmers
concepts.summary: Why a store on this core is not yet a load on that one.
objectives: Explain why a store on this core is not yet a load on that one
Predict a reordering that surprises a program that assumed a single global order

concepts.name: Semaphores
concepts.summary: A counter you can wait on.
objectives: Describe a semaphore as a counter you can wait on
Predict how a semaphore of count N lets N holders through

concepts.name: Condition variables
concepts.summary: Sleep until someone says the world changed.
objectives: Describe a condition variable as sleeping until someone says the world changed
Predict why waiting on a condvar must re-check the condition after wakeup
